instrument: Washington County BCC Work Session, September 1, 2026, staff presentation
summary: Per county staff: an Oregon land use moratorium requires findings of need and resources for regulatory updates, 45-day notice to DLCD before the final hearing, lasts at most 120 days, and may be extended up to six months on a showing of progress. Staff's hypothetical timeline ran from Board direction September 1 to a moratorium expiring February 18, 2027. The Board did not proceed.
text: A moratorium (pause) on a particular land use is allowed by state statute, provided that the local jurisdiction can make findings of the need to impose a moratorium and that resources are available to make necessary regulatory updates. Statute requires a minimum 45-day notice to the state Department of Land Conservation and Development (DLCD) prior to the final public hearing to consider adoption; The moratorium can last for a maximum of 120 days; It may be extended for up to six additional months if the jurisdiction can show progress towards regulatory updates; the extension process requires a notice period, a public hearing, and findings
